title: Uniform compression of minimum feasible extension energy proposes adaptive convex interface queries and design
reported_status: Source-reported mathematical arguments only. Intake checked byte preservation and repository structure; no independent proof reconstruction, scientific-code replay, citation verification, formal proof, quantum circuit execution, or experimental validation was performed. External correctness and historical priority remain UNKNOWN. The supplied verify_constraint_power.py and verification_results (1).json report 129 exact support-kernel checks, 40 conditional-energy identities, 24 floating full/reduced convex-design problems, coefficients down to 2^-200 and one full-state recovery diagnostic. The diagnostic has 6 state entries and 64 sketch rows; observed worst geometry distortion about35.9%. It demonstrates no compression at scale or theorem-wide tolerance. Neither artifact was executed at intake.
scientific_scope_status: The rational input supplies a fixed SPD quadratic host H=G^T W G (positive diagonal W), full-row-rank conservation matrix A, independent-column load basis F and M candidate measurements Cx. A query chooses |S|<=k and an explicit rational polyhedron in (C_Sx,a,z), with a nonnegative objective psi having an explicit convex-QP formulation, to minimize x^T Hx+psi subject to Ax=Fa. Arbitrary nonlinear functions are not free optimization oracles. The source proposes q=O([k log(eM/k)+log(1/delta)]/epsilon^2) random response rows plus d load responses, giving one simultaneous 1-delta guarantee for every support and adaptive query: exact local feasibility, relative optimal value and near-optimal feasible extension. Online arithmetic is O(qk^2+kd+d^2) plus one QP in O(k+d+dim z) variables, with its bit complexity charged. This remains a derived unreviewed algorithmic candidate, not a general nonlinear mechanics or unrestricted topology solver.
